speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are experiencing fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes. To begin narrowing down the cause, have you noticed any changes in your bowel movements or stool appearance recently?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Those symptoms are concerning; the combination of night sweats, weight loss, and supraclavicular lymphadenopathy suggests a systemic issue. Can you tell me if you have any history of abdominal masses, lumps, or recent fevers, and have you noticed any bleeding or bruising? REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, LDH, ESR.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: COMPLETE_BLOOD_COUNT: WBC: Elevated, Hemoglobin: Slightly Decreased, Platelets: Normal; LACTATE_DEHYDROGENASE (LDH): Elevated; ESR: Normal Readings

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Patient
text: I also feel fullness in my abdomen and my clothes feel tighter. I do not have cough or recent travel.

speaker: Patient
text: I have smoked about one pack a day for many years, and I drink socially. The abdominal discomfort and fatigue have both been getting worse. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: The history of heavy smoking combined with weight loss, night sweats, and supraclavicular lymphadenopathy is highly concerning for lung or abdominal malignancy; have you noticed any cough, hemoptysis, or loss of appetite? REQUEST TEST: CT Chest and Abdomen, CA 19-9.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CT_SCAN_THORAX_AND_ABDOMEN: Massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes; CA_19-9: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma (likely Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma). The imaging confirms extensive lymphadenopathy in cervical, axillary, and mediastinal regions with normal CA 19-9, which effectively rules out pancreatic or biliary adenocarcinoma given the constitutional symptoms of B-symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss).
